title: Why Rereading Feels Productive but Doesn't Stick

titles.option_a_curiosity: Why Rereading Feels Productive but Doesn't Stick
titles.option_b_contrarian: The Study Habit That Fools Your Brain
titles.option_c_search_hybrid: Retrieval Practice: The Study Method Evidence Backs

description:
Rereading a chapter feels like studying, but familiarity is not the same as recall. This Short follows a student from a failed quiz to the methods cognitive research supports most. The video shows why closing the book and answering a question from memory strengthens the path back to a fact, while highlighting and rereading mainly build familiarity. It explains that the struggle of retrieving an answer and then checking it is the useful part, and that revisiting the material across days makes that practice more durable. Rereading still helps you understand a passage; it simply does not rehearse recall, so it should not be mistaken for a test of what you know. The takeaway is to measure study time by the answers you can produce with the book shut, not by the number of pages you turned.
